# Conclusions

In this review, we have discussed the role of NK cells in the tumor immune surveillance system, with an emphasis on cancer immunotherapy targeting NK cells. Although much progress has been made in the last several years, the role of NK cells in anti-tumor immune surveillance is not fully understood. More studies on NK cell subsets, NK ligands and receptors, as well as the role of microenvironment, cytokines and NK subsets under the influence of cytokine environment in modulating NK cell activity will improve our understanding of NK cell biology

# Background

The interaction between drugs and targets is one of the key mechanisms of action and the potential treatment targets of most drugs. Identifying new drugs from existing drugs and the associated interactions with targets is a popular and practical task in drug discovery. Although a number of approaches have been developed to find novel drugs with the consideration of drugs and targets, the accuracy of these approaches is still unsatisfactory.
